FAQ
For first-time visitors
What is this app, in plain words?
It is a movie-first way to explore how a film affects a person, a business, a community, and the wider economy.
Do I need to understand economics to use it?
No. The app should make the idea understandable through simple language, visuals, and guided steps.
What are the main pages?
Individual, Micro, Macro, and Community. Each page tells one part of the same story.
How to read the numbers
Are all the numbers exact?
No. Some are exact formulas, like the macro identities. Others are story indicators that help people understand the experience.
Why use movies?
Because movies are emotional, social, and easy to remember. They make complex ideas feel concrete.
What should I trust most?
Trust the labels, the formula structure, and the notes that say whether something is a canonical measure or a story metric.
Still being refined
What is still changing?
The exact wording of some story metrics, the helper text, and the way we explain the logic to new users.
Should I treat this as financial advice or a strict economic ledger?
No. It is a storytelling and translation layer. The real accounting and protocol truth stay in the underlying canon and docs.
Assumptions and boundaries
The front end is a translation layer, not a replacement for the spec.
Storytelling is allowed, but the underlying economics and protocol logic should remain honest.
A movie can be read as a personal, business, macroeconomic, and communal event at the same time.
Some metrics are exact identities; others are qualitative indicators designed to help people understand the experience.
All wellbeing-related displays should remain normalized around 1.0 in the live model.
Why this exists

The goal is honesty: keep the story rich and visual, but never hide the logic. If a number is a story metric, it should say so. If a formula is canonical, it should stay canonical.
